shared_implementation: The companion owns folder proofs independently of the browser orchestration. Abandoned proof cleanup uses the same bounded Coordinator and native OS folder gate as accepted workspace operations. This native primitive serves the shared folder/resource facade; feature and transaction policy remain in the existing shared interpreter.
contract: Proof creation and explicit prove/close cleanup borrow their current native folder lease. Successful explicit cleanup disarms the destructor.

Expiry, supersession, unrelated-root sweeping and host drop transfer the original captured proof to a registered bounded native worker. The worker acquires that proof folder before checking its inode and secret and removing the file.

No deletion runs directly from Drop. A missing runtime, shutdown, exhausted worker/queue/handle capacity, changed physical folder or failed lock acquisition preserves the proof. Registration precedes spawning, so shutdown includes admitted cleanup.
Cleanup rechecks the proof after waiting. Changed contents, replacement inodes and replacement folder paths are preserved. It does not borrow an unrelated request folder gate.
The OS ancestor/root lock set excludes nested folders and physical aliases across cooperating bridge processes. A frozen owner retains its lock; proof expiry never steals ownership by age.
coverage: Before the fix, a real HTTP folder session expired after 45 seconds and its proof was deleted while a separate Python process still held an exclusive native lock on the actual directory.
The same actual HTTP expiry contract now holds the proof unchanged across expiry, releases the foreign lock and requires cleanup to finish afterward on the matching rebuilt bridge binary.

Eight native regressions cover original-gate waiting, sweep under an unrelated gate, host drop, later contents and replacement inodes, changed folder paths, shutdown and full worker capacity, stopped runtime, and another process holding an ancestor through a symlink alias.
Existing prove/close behavior, exact proof identity/content preservation and full bridge unit, integration and documentation suites remain covered on macOS and Linux.
